analysis:
The PR changes only docs/reference/protocol-messages.md: the 'Last updated' date (line 3), the performance_measurements age semantics (head line 578, now measured since the newest observation even if an older completed sample arrives later), and a new paragraph (lines 580-584) saying the Swift producer applies the same age rule to each workload bucket and current-posture series in EnginePerformanceMeasurements.swift. It states explicitly that wire fields are unchanged. No code, authorization, encryption, attestation or routing logic changes in this diff.

Threat-model relevance: performance_measurements are untrusted provider-supplied routing observations (TB-002). The documented change is about freshness accounting and does not affect the App Attest authorization path (TB-011, T-053..T-058), endpoint-resumption custody, drain barrier, or trust gates. The existing doc text, such as the resume section at lines 47-109, still matches TB-011: it is not a bearer grant, grants no local trust, and answers only on the originating socket. It introduces no new attack surface or invalidated assumption.

Open integration questions: the Swift implementation (EnginePerformanceMeasurements.swift) and the Go clamp/freshness code are not in the supplied evidence, so I could not verify that the code matches the doc. A provider could misreport sample_age_ms to look fresher, but this is pre-existing, advisory telemetry, and the doc says it does not gate routing. No findings.
